note: The curated tier: places with a reason to care. This is the voice, and it is hand-written. Empty is honest; generated would not be.

items.title: Rim Naam
items.why: Thai, served in a wooden pavilion that sits out over a lily pond in the Oberoi's gardens, under a rain tree — Rim Naam means "by the water". The kitchen is run by Chef Tam, from Isan, and it cooks Thai food properly rather than politely. Lean towards the seafood and the curries. Go for dinner, when the garden is lit and the city has gone quiet around it.

items.title: Nāvu
items.why: A small fine-dining room on MG Road that only opens for dinner. Book ahead, go without a plan and let the menu do the work — this is a place for a long evening, not a quick bite.

items.title: Middle Room
items.why: A 33-seat listening bar in The Courtyard, built around sound equipment and vinyl brought back from Tokyo. The deal is beer, a good record and a room where people actually listen. Go in a pair, not a group, and not to talk over it.

items.title: Cameo
items.area: Museum of Art & Photography, Kasturba Road
items.why: Two rooms in the Museum of Art & Photography: Bistro Cameo downstairs, and Bar Cameo, a rooftop bar that turns the museum into an evening out. Do the galleries in the late afternoon, then go up for a drink as it gets dark.

items.title: Brine
items.why: A big, brutalist bar-restaurant on 80 Feet Road where the cocktails are the experiment — yes, there is a cheese one — and the food is comfort. Order the burger and something odd from the bar.

items.title: Knowhere
items.area: Favourite Plaza, Dodda Banaswadi Main Road
items.why: A neighbourhood rooftop bar and grill, five floors up in Banaswadi. Beer, cocktails and comfort food, and karaoke once a week if that is your kind of night. Unpretentious, which is the point.

items.title: Kabab Korner
items.why: A St Mark's Road takeaway for kebabs and rolls, the thing to eat standing up between two bars on this stretch. Order a roll and a plate of kebabs; do not expect a table.

items.title: Lapis
items.why: The Oberoi's all-day restaurant, named for its lapis-blue ceiling, with a patio beside the water and a deck in the hotel gardens. The wood-fired oven carries the lunch buffet. At dinner, order from the grill or the house pasta and sit outside.

items.title: Wabi Sabi
items.why: The Oberoi's Japanese and Nikkei restaurant: slate walls, a gold-leaf wall, the sound of a waterfall. Order sushi, sashimi and the ceviche. This is a place for an occasion, and the bill says so.

items.title: Byg Brewski Brewing Company
items.area: Sarjapur Main Road, near the Wipro corporate office
items.why: The Sarjapur Road branch of the Byg Brewski brewpubs: big, mostly outdoors, and made for a long evening with a group. Drink what they brew on site, get a table on the lawn, and plan to stay a while.
items.coordsFrom: OpenStreetMap way/370327479 (Wipro Corporate Office, next door; approximate)

items.title: Byg Brewski Brewing Company
items.why: The Hennur flagship, billed as the biggest brewpub in Asia: 65,000 square feet, room for thousands, lawns and several separate bars. It is a destination, not a local, so go with a group and a free evening, and drink what they brew on site.
items.coordsFrom: OpenStreetMap way/43102213 (Southern Asia Bible College, next door; approximate)

items.title: Maverick & Farmer Coffee
items.why: The flagship of a coffee company with its own estate in Coorg, near Ulsoor Lake. The menu runs from espresso classics to the experimental. Order one of each, with something from the kitchen, and take a slow morning over it.

items.title: Bhavani Koffee
items.area: 8th Cross, by the Kannika Parameshwari Temple
items.why: A coffee roaster and powder shop running since 1965, now with a counter for drinking it. Have a filter coffee standing up, then buy a bag of their blend ground fresh to take home. Pair it with a walk down 8th Cross market.
items.coordsFrom: OpenStreetMap way/1338319141 (Kannika Parameshwari Temple, next door; approximate)

items.title: Nerlu Café
items.area: Crescent Road, off Race Course Road
items.why: A café built as a tasting room for Indian coffee — nerlu means shade in Kannada, where arabica likes to grow. There is a changing menu of ten roasters. Choose three, have them brewed side by side, and they will put you in touch with the roaster whose coffee you liked. There is a bakery and kitchen too, and seats outside.

items.title: Lakeview Milk Bar
items.why: An MG Road institution since 1930. It began as an Englishman's ice-cream cart overlooking Ulsoor Lake, and in 1947 he sold it to a nineteen-year-old from the city. Order a sundae or a thick milkshake. It is the old Bengaluru way to end an evening on MG Road.
items.source: The News Minute; Deccan Herald; lakeviewmilkbar.in

items.title: Fabelle – The Chocolate Boutique
items.why: The first Fabelle boutique, inside ITC Gardenia, where chocolatiers make the desserts and cocoa drinks in front of you. Order a plated chocolate dessert and a hot chocolate, then pick up a box of the filled chocolates on the way out.

items.title: Maison du Brownie & Cheese Cake
items.why: A small Indiranagar counter that does two things: cheesecake and brownies. The Basque cheesecake is the order. It stays open late for takeaway, when most dessert places have shut.

items.title: La Couronne Patisserie and Cafe
items.why: A French-style patisserie on Cunningham Road: glossy entremets, tarts and a café to eat them in. Order one of the showpiece pastries with a coffee in the afternoon.

items.title: Churroland
items.why: Billed as Bangalore's first churro shop: churros fried to order, with dips, filled tubs or loaded into sundaes. Order the classic churros with chocolate and eat them while they are hot. It is open late enough to be the end of an evening.

items.title: Echo Cocktail & Tapas Bar
items.area: Aloft, Cessna Business Park, Outer Ring Road
items.why: A rooftop bar at the Aloft on the Outer Ring Road, with a gin list of more than thirty brands, tapas to go with it, and live bands or DJs on busy nights. Go at sunset and order a gin and tonic built on something you have not tried.
items.coordsFrom: OpenStreetMap way/347475248 (Aloft Bengaluru Cessna Business Park)

items.title: Beanlore Coffee Roasters
items.area: Doddanakundi Industrial Area, off ITPB Road
items.why: Whitefield's specialty roaster, with single-origin Indian coffees, pour-overs, and a quiet room built for working in. Order a pour-over of whatever they roasted this week. There is Thai curry at lunch if you are staying.

items.title: Dose Manjanna
items.why: A Jayanagar dosa counter named after the man at the tawa. Soft, butter-heavy dosas and fluffy idlis. Order the benne dose, eat it hot, and follow it with a filter coffee.
items.coordsFrom: OpenStreetMap way/1242203419 (Garuda Swagath Mall, next door; approximate)

items.title: Sankey Tank
items.why: A lake from the 1880s with a walking path round it, between Malleshwaram and Sadashivanagar. Walk the loop at sunrise or sunset, when the whole neighbourhood comes out, then go for coffee in Malleshwaram.

items.title: Orion Mall
items.why: A big mall at Brigade Gateway, with a lakeside promenade behind it, a multiplex and a long food court. Useful on a rainy afternoon, and for a film. The walk by the lake is the best part.

items.title: K-Soul Cafe
items.why: A self-serve Korean ramen bar modelled on a Seoul convenience store. Pick a packet of ramyeon off the shelf and cook it yourself at the machine in four minutes, then finish with a milk mochi or a Korean ice cream. It is closed on Mondays.

items.title: Neko & Matcha
items.why: A Japanese-style matcha café that is also a cat café. Order a matcha latte, sit on the floor, and let the cats decide whether to come over.

items.title: Amadora
items.why: Small-batch artisanal ice cream from Chennai, with unusual flavours next to very good classics. Ask to taste two or three before you choose.
